# Vector Symbolic Architectures and Hyperdimensional Computing {#sec-ch-vector-symbolic-architectures}

This chapter is a stub. Its outline follows the roadmap in [index.qmd](../index.qmd) and exists so that other chapters can already cross-reference its sections.

## Near-Orthogonality as a Resource
*The payoff of @sec-ch-curse-of-dimensionality, representing concepts directly in 10,000-dimensional hypervectors.*

## Algebraic Operations on Thoughts

### Bundling ($+$)
*Superposition and set representation. Bundling is commutative, like Chomsky's Merge (1995), the single operation of the Minimalist Program, which builds the unordered set $\{a, b\}$; in both, order and hierarchy must come from somewhere else, binding and permutation here and labelling there.*

### Binding ($\odot$ / $\circledast$)
*Role-filler pairing and circular convolution. Modality is a natural role: a multimodal percept is the bundle of bindings of a modality with its content, so that a photograph, a bark, and a gait can be superposed in one hypervector and still be told apart.*

### Permutation ($\Pi$)
*Sequence ordering and hierarchical encoding.*

## Associative Clean-Up Memories & Capacity Bounds
*Theoretical bounds on robust concept retrieval without weight retraining, and the relation to attention as associative memory.*

## Scale Test
*Capacity grows with dimension, and dimension is cheap. When does a hyperdimensional encoding beat a learned one?*
